title.label: Not reliable notifying about new posts

content.label:
This app is useful for keeping up to date with loved ones who are going through a rough time and don’t want to use other social media platforms, but it is really bad at reliably notifying you about new posts even when everything is setup correctly. This would be less frustrating if the app wasn’t constantly sending notifications asking you for money (something you cannot turn off). That feels unearned when it is not fulfilling its most essential function.
The immediate ask for a donation when you create an account and follow someone would feel less predatory if it was more clear that the support donation was going to the platform and not the patient. I understand they have to keep the lights on and this is a delicate balance, but it deserves another careful look at exactly how and when these messages are implemented so you’re not taking advantage of the desperation of the situation.

title.label: Helpful App - Sharing on iPad Not Working

content.label:
CaringBridge is a wonderful service and we appreciate it so much, especially in this time when our family has a member who has a life-changing medical condition. I offer this feedback as an opportunity for improvement and not a judgment.

When I share an update on my iPhone, the full action dialogue opens with all options available. On my iPad, I am presented with a tooltip and only the action dialogue header with the name of the app appears with no actions. I have looked to see if there is an option I have not enabled, but I can find none. I believe it may be a bug due to the tooltip container.

One other issue is that the app freezes in an auto-save mode which never resolves. I have to copy any content to the pasteboard or another app and force-quit. Once relaunched, there seems to be a window of time before it happens again. I paste the content and send before that happens usually. If I am interrupted, which can happen frequently for a caregiver, the issue reoccurs.

We are grateful for this app and this service. Thank you.

title.label: Your website is more and more annoying!!!

content.label:
Update to my earlier comments:
Since posting the review below, I have received daily, repetitive emails from Apple that have the same response from the developer of Caring Bridge. So far, 10 identical emails. The emails invite me to update my review. And each one has the same auto-generated comment from CB. I chalk up this repetition to just another software glitch on the CB side. Meanwhile, I’ve also read through many comments on the site posted by other people. I see I am not alone. Many complaints about the flow of the website, notifications not working, and too many requests for donations. And that same generic message gets repeated on most of these reviews. 

My original message:
I have notifications set up so that I know when there is a new update from friends whose serious illness I am worried about. But first, I have to plow through your asks for a donation on every visit to the site. Even though I recently GAVE money to Caring Bridge. And I get more and more fundraising asks by notification. These are NOT the notifications I have agreed to. Now I feel I must remove all notifications, which means I may miss important information about my friends!

I have had five years of FSGS, two and a half years of dialysis and three people trying to donate a kidney but being unable to due to health reasons. Literally hundreds of people have been praying for us, some I’ve never met!
Once we got the call and we were hustling to get from Greenville SC to Mayo in Minnesota ASAP the CaringBridge site provided the most effective and efficient way to communicate with anyone who desired information and updates. 
It has been a whirlwind week. My recovery is ahead of schedule and my doctors are all pleased. 
FIVE STARS AND THANK YOU CARINGBRIDGE!! ❤️😇🎯
Joel and Ann Shaw
Greenville SC
